content_of_post_to_comment:
This is going to be a long post so bear with me.
PS: Used Chatgpt to frame the wording better

I’m a creative professional with 15 years of experience.

I started freelancing in 2014 because I never wanted a conventional 9-to-5 job. I valued freedom, creative control, and the ability to work on my own terms. Freelancing went well financially, but I eventually quit in 2021 because I was getting married in 2024 and my future in-laws viewed freelancing as less legitimate than a conventional job. I joined a small overseas company as a full-time remote employee, working from another country closer to my parents.

The job initially gave me exactly what I needed: good pay, excellent work-life balance, freedom, flexible hours, and regular increments. I also had savings, income from trading, occasional freelance work, and a YouTube channel that has grown to 51K+ subscribers.

Then AI changed everything in late 2022. The company shifted heavily toward AI, and although I enjoyed learning it, the workload increased dramatically without anyone being added to my department. I became responsible for almost the entire creative output. By 2025, I was sometimes producing five videos a day.

The work became increasingly repetitive and reactive. My founder often sent me things he saw online and asked me to recreate them. I felt like I was executing rather than creating. This gradually destroyed my motivation and took a serious mental toll. I became anxious about work, constantly thinking about what new thing I would have to learn or reproduce next.

Ironically, the projects I’m most proud of were the ones where I had complete creative freedom, direct client access, and enough time to think. Those projects went extremely well and showed me that the problem was never my ability to create. It was the environment I was creating in.

By 2024-25, I was exhausted, anxious, struggling with sleep, and mentally checked out. I eventually decided to quit in July 2026. The plan was simple: build my YouTube channel, take selective freelance work, and spend my time creating things I actually care about.

For about a month, I felt motivated. I made several videos combining AI and traditional animation, but they averaged around 800 views. I also started a separate educational channel, which has remained stagnant.

That has created a new problem.

Now whenever I get an idea, my first thought is: “What’s the point of making this if it isn’t going to earn anything?”

I want to make useful long-form content around education, science, history, and current affairs. But low-effort AI content performs far better on my Instagram, and although I could easily chase that, I don’t want to build my career around AI slop.

For the last two months, my routine has become frustratingly stagnant. I wake up with little motivation and a heavy head, work out with my wife, sit at my computer, open a project, and within minutes find myself browsing instead of working. Sometimes I take a nap, wake up feeling better, and finish in an hour what I struggled with for an entire day.

I often get bursts of motivation while showering, but they disappear when I sit down to work.

I’ve also started feeling frustrated about not having enough mental space or solitude. My wife is supportive and doesn’t interrupt my work, but having another person constantly around makes me feel like I never truly switch into my own space. What confuses me is that even when she is out, I often still cannot make myself work.

That’s where I am now.

I used to be someone who constantly experimented, took risks, learned new things, freelanced, travelled, created, and figured things out along the way.

Now I feel stuck between wanting creative freedom and needing my work to have financial meaning.

I don’t think I’ve lost my ability to create. I think I’ve lost the drive to create without knowing where it is going.

And I’m trying to figure out how to become that version of myself again.

EDIT: I work alone as I have no friends in same field as I have to discuss. I used to be always self motivated.
comment: The part about your best work happening when you had creative freedom and direct client access stood out to me. It sounds less like you've lost motivation and more like you've trained yourself to associate creating with pressure and performance metrics. Maybe rebuilding that creative muscle means making a few things with no audience or income goal attached, just to prove that the process can feel rewarding again.
